Meta.title: Voxa — Dub any video, keep it in sync
Meta.description: Open-source AI video dubbing. Whisper transcription, context-aware LLM translation, four TTS engines, and placement locked to the speaker. MIT-licensed. Runs on your machine.

Why.label: Why Voxa
Why.title: The dub never falls behind the speaker.
Why.body: Naive tools concatenate clips and drift. Voxa anchors every clip to the source timeline, so the dub stays locked to the speaker — no growing lag, no re-syncing by hand.

Features.label: Features
Features.title: Everything the pipeline needs
Features.subtitle: A complete dubbing toolchain — transcription to final mux — in a single command.

items.title: Anchored placement
items.body: Every clip is pinned to the source timeline. Drift stays at zero.

items.title: Four TTS engines
items.body: Edge, OpenAI, Piper (offline), and XTTS voice cloning.

items.title: Context-aware translation
items.body: Google, Ollama, OpenAI, or Anthropic — translate with full-sentence context.

items.title: Quality gate
items.body: Optional WER scoring re-synthesizes lines that miss the mark.

items.title: Self-hostable
items.body: Point any OpenAI-compatible TTS endpoint with --openai-tts-base-url.

items.title: Resumable
items.body: Checkpoints let you stop and pick up exactly where you left off.

HowItWorks.label: How it works
HowItWorks.title: Seven steps, one command
HowItWorks.subtitle: Voxa runs a deterministic pipeline from raw audio to a synced dub.

steps.title: Extract audio
steps.body: Pull the audio track from the source video with ffmpeg.

steps.title: Denoise
steps.body: Clean background noise so transcription stays accurate.

steps.title: Transcribe
steps.body: Whisper turns speech into timed text.

steps.title: Merge sentences
steps.body: Group fragments into natural, translatable sentences.

steps.title: Translate
steps.body: An LLM translates with full-sentence context.

steps.title: Synthesize
steps.body: The chosen TTS engine speaks each line.

steps.title: Mux
steps.body: Anchor every clip to the timeline and remux the video.

Install.label: Installation
Install.title: Install Voxa
Install.subtitle: Download the installer on Windows, or install with one line on any system. Either way you get Voxa, the Python it runs on and, on Windows and macOS, FFmpeg, with a Voxa Studio shortcut.
Install.setupBody: An installer for your user alone, with no administrator rights. It puts Voxa, the Python it runs on and Voxa Studio in one folder, adds a Start menu shortcut, installs FFmpeg with winget if it's missing, and appears in Apps & features to uninstall.
Install.setupSize: 11 MB to download, always the newest release. As it installs, it fetches the rest, about 1 GB, most of it PyTorch.
Install.setupUnsigned: It isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may say “Windows protected your PC”: choose More info, then Run anyway. Your browser may also ask whether to keep the file.
Install.oneLine: Or with one line, on any system
Install.note: Already have Python? pipx install "voxa-dub[serve]" works too. voxa doctor shows what is ready and what is missing.

items.q: Does the dub drift out of sync?
items.a: No. Voxa anchors every clip to the source timeline, so placement stays locked to the speaker.
Yes — Whisper locally, Ollama for translation, and Piper for speech. No cloud calls required.

items.q: Can I use my own TTS server?
items.a: Yes. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works via --openai-tts-base-url.
Whisper covers around 100 source languages; targets depend on the TTS engine you choose.
Yes, Voxa is MIT-licensed. The engines and voices it drives carry their own licenses, and some offline voices are non-commercial, so check NOTICE.md before commercial use.

Author.label: Author
Author.title: Built by Servoogle
Author.body: Voxa is an open-source project by Servoogle, created and maintained by Akshin Miranov — practical, self-hostable tools with no lock-in and no telemetry.

translation.title: Translation style
translation.desc: Extra guidance for LLM translators (OpenAI, Anthropic), layered on top of the built-in prompt. The output format, line count and timing rules always stay enforced.
translation.placeholder: e.g. Formal register for a medical audience. Keep terminology precise. Brand voice: warm and concise.
translation.hint: Applies to OpenAI/Anthropic translation only. Leave empty for the default behaviour.

speech.title: Speech style
speech.desc: How the dubbed voice should sound with OpenAI TTS. Combine presets, add your own direction, or both.
speech.placeholder: e.g. Like a nature documentary narrator. Confident, never rushed.
speech.guard: Timing is always enforced: Voxa appends a locked instruction for steady, natural pacing with no added pauses. Style changes how the voice sounds — never how long a line takes, so the dub stays in sync.

advanced.deviceHint: Whisper, diarization and the local voices. Automatic uses an NVIDIA GPU when there is one, else the CPU.
advanced.deviceMpsHint: Experimental: Whisper, diarization, Chatterbox and Demucs try Apple's GPU and fall back to the CPU if they fail there; XTTS, VoxCPM2 and faster-whisper stay on the CPU. Tell us how it goes.
advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.desc: Reliability and timing knobs for power users. The defaults are recommended.
advanced.fallbackHint: If the main translator fails on most lines (an outage, a bad key, or Google turning your network away), those lines are retried with this one.
advanced.rateHint: How much translated text is budgeted per second. Default 15; range 8–30. Lower condenses more, higher rushes delivery.
advanced.workersHint: How many segments the cloud engines (OpenAI, Edge) synthesize at once. Default 4; range 1–16. Higher is faster but may hit your API rate limit. Offline engines ignore it.
advanced.concurrentHint: How many jobs run in parallel instead of queueing. Default 1; range 1–4. Raising it helps when the engines wait on the network (cloud translation and speech) and costs memory when they don't — each job loads its own Whisper model. Two dubs of the same video always run one after the other.
advanced.qualityGateHint: Scores each synthesized line and re-renders a garbled one with neutral delivery. Slower, OpenAI TTS. Off by default.
advanced.autoDownloadHint: When a job finishes, its video is saved to your downloads folder without clicking Download. Only works while the console is open, and your browser may ask permission before saving several files at once.
advanced.checkUpdatesHint: Once a day, Voxa asks PyPI which voxa-dub is the newest and tells you here when it's newer than yours. PyPI sees what any download shows it (your IP address) and this Voxa's version; nothing about your videos or settings is sent. VOXA_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 turns it off for the command line as well.
